```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

The current release covers Swedish electoral events from 2002 onwards,
including elections to the Riksdag, regional and municipal councils and the
European Parliament, as well as the 2003 national referendum on the euro
and re-elections.
This guide introduces results, seats, mandate-period changes, preference votes
and re-elections; see [Coverage](coverage.html) for available years and functions.
Install the current package release, v0.4.1, from GitHub. The `nanoparquet`
package reads canonical data:

```{r installation}
install.packages(c("remotes", "nanoparquet"))
remotes::install_github("richardohrvall/swelections", ref = "v0.4.1")
library(swelections)
```

These examples use published canonical data and need no local raw-data archive.
Files are downloaded when first needed. See [Coverage](coverage.html) for
availability and [Accessing the data](accessing-data.html) for source choices.

## Results and geographic levels

`results()` supports national (`"national"`), county (`"county"`), regional
(`"region"`), municipal (`"municipality"`) and voting-district (`"district"`)
results. Constituency levels are `"parliamentary_constituency"`,
`"regional_constituency"` and `"municipal_constituency"`, depending on the
election. Constituencies are electoral areas for the relevant parliament or
council. Available levels vary by election, year and counting stage.
For a brief introduction to the Swedish electoral system and the geographic
and institutional features relevant to these data, see
[Understanding Swedish elections](understanding-elections.html).

For example, read the final 2022 parliamentary result nationally or by voting
district:

```{r results}
national <- results(year = 2022, election = "parliamentary", level = "national")
head(national)

districts <- results(year = 2022, election = "parliamentary", level = "district")
head(districts)
```

Choose one level for an analysis. Totals such as ballots cast can repeat across
party rows; do not sum those repeated totals or add different geographic levels
together. See [Standard and full detail](coverage.html#standard-and-full-detail)
for the difference between the default output and `detail = "full"`.

## Seats

Read municipal seat allocations:

```{r seats}
municipal_seats <- seats(year = 2022, election = "municipal", level = "municipality")
head(municipal_seats)
```

`seats()` describes the allocation made at an election.

## Mandate-period changes

An election establishes an initial allocation, but mandate holders can change
during the period. `mandate_history()` describes holder and vacancy intervals;
`members_at()` returns the people holding mandates on a date; and
`vacant_seats_at()` returns verified vacancies on that date.

```{r mandate-changes}
history <- mandate_history(year = 2018, election = "parliamentary")
head(history)

members <- members_at(date = "2020-01-01", year = 2018, election = "parliamentary")
head(members)
```

All three functions use the same population of allocated mandates. They describe
formal mandate holding under the sources' date conventions, not attendance at
meetings or temporary substitute service. See
[Coverage](coverage.html#mandate-period-history) for supported mandate periods.

## Preference votes

Examine national preference votes in the 2024 European Parliament election:

```{r preferences}
personal <- preference_votes(year = 2024, election = "european", level = "national")
head(personal)
```

Candidate numbers identify source records and must not be used to link people
across elections. Names may be missing even when preference votes are reported.

## Re-elections

Discover separate re-election events without downloading results:

```{r events, eval=TRUE}
library(swelections)
election_events(election_kind = "re_election")
```

Then request Falun's 2019 re-election result:

```{r falun}
falun <- results(
  year = 2019,
  election = "municipal",
  election_kind = "re_election"
)
head(falun)
```

A re-election is a separate event within the original mandate period. It does
not start a new ordinary election series or mandate period. See
[Coverage](coverage.html#re-elections) for supported re-election functions.

## Sources and language

The default `source = "auto"` is recommended for most users. It chooses approved
canonical data first, otherwise a supported remote source; never a local raw
archive. Choose a source explicitly when you need a particular input. See
[Accessing the data](accessing-data.html#source-selection-in-r) for explicit
source choices.

English functions use English column names and technical categories by default. All seven election-data functions and
all three mandate-period functions also accept `names = "sv"` to return Swedish
column names and technical categories. This does not translate all text from
the source material. Proper names and literal source identifiers retain their
source spelling.

Swedish function names provide corresponding interfaces, for example
`valresultat()` for `results()`, `mandat()` for `seats()` and `personroster()` for
`preference_votes()`. `election_events()` is the exception: it has no `names`
argument. Use its Swedish counterpart `valtillfallen()` for Swedish event metadata.

See [Reference](../reference/index.html) for arguments and output definitions.
